## Purpose
The frontend's single HTTP API client — every backend REST call (auth, chat, workflow runs, analytics, admin, user preferences, capabilities, gate/answer/cancel/resume/revision commands) is a thin exported function in this file, built on `fetch` with JWT bearer-token auth.

## Shape
- `getToken` / `setToken` / `clearToken` / `logout`: JWT token management against `localStorage`.
- `request<T>()`: the shared fetch wrapper — builds the URL from `BASE_URL`, wraps every call in an `AbortController` with a 30s timeout, and throws a typed `ApiError` (status + detail) on both non-2xx responses and timeouts/network errors.
- `authHeaders()`: builds the `Content-Type`/`Authorization` header pair used by nearly every call.
- Per-domain exported functions grouped under `// ---` comment banners: Auth API, Chat API, Workflow API, Analytics API, Run command API (gate/cancel/resume/answers/revision), Admin API, User Preferences API, Capabilities API, Saved Workflows API, plus normalizer helpers (`normalizeChatSession`, `normalizeWorkflowRun`, `ensureUTC`) that reshape raw backend JSON into the frontend's typed models.
- `ApiError` class carrying `status` and `detail` so callers can branch on HTTP status.

## Why this shape
The file is a flat, function-per-endpoint client rather than a class or generated SDK — a comment on `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` explains the timeout exists specifically because the browser's ~6-connection-per-origin pool can be saturated by per-run SSE streams, which would otherwise hang a request forever with no visible error; wrapping every call through the shared `request()` helper centralizes that fail-fast behavior and error typing for all endpoints at once.
